info.title: Facebook Clone API
info.description:
REST API for the Facebook clone: accounts, posts, reels, reactions, comments, friends, groups, messages and stories.

**Signing in:** call `POST /auth/register` or `POST /auth/login`, copy the `token` from the response, then press **Authorize** above and paste it. Every route except register and login needs it.

**Reels are posts.** A reel is a post with `type: "reel"` and exactly one video, so posts and reels share the same endpoints, including comments and reactions.

**Realtime.** Open a WebSocket to `ws://localhost:3000/ws` and send `{ "type": "auth", "token": "<jwt>", "lastEventId": "<id or null>" }` as the first frame. The server answers `{ "type": "ready", "data": { "userId", "resync" } }`.

Events about you carry an `id` (`message:new`, `message:updated`, `message:hidden`, `conversation:read`, `conversation:updated`, `conversation:removed`, `notification:new`, `notification:read`, `notification:removed`, `friends:changed`). Send the last id you saw when reconnecting: anything you missed in the last five minutes is replayed right after `ready`. When `resync` is true the gap could not be covered, so refetch over REST.

Live-only events have no id and are never replayed: `typing`, `presence:changed` (friends only), and, for posts you subscribe to, `comment:new`, `comment:deleted` and `post:reactions`.

After `ready` a client may send `{ "type": "typing", "conversationId" }`, `{ "type": "subscribe", "topic": "post:<id>" }` and `{ "type": "unsubscribe", "topic" }`. Subscriptions are checked against who may read the post. Every write still goes through these REST routes.

Close codes: 1008 more than 40 frames in 10 seconds, 1011 realtime unavailable, 4001 bad, expired or revoked token, 4002 no auth frame within 5 seconds, 4003 account deactivated.

Set `REDIS_URL` to run several backend instances: events, presence and the replay log then go through Redis 7+ instead of process memory.

**Rate limits:** `/api/auth/*` allows 20 requests per 15 minutes per IP; everything else allows 500.

errors.description: Present on validation failures: one message per field.

example.email: Please provide a valid email address.

token.description: JWT, valid for JWT_EXPIRES_IN (7d by default).

Person.description: A trimmed user, used by friend lists and suggestions.

Reactions.description: Tally of a post's reactions plus the reaction of the caller.

counts.description: How many people picked each reaction type.

viewerReaction.description: The caller's own reaction, or null.

title.example: Small moments from a slow morning.

groupId.description: Set when the post belongs to a group; null for the main feed.

FriendEdge.description: One friendship row, seen from the caller's side.

id.description: Friendship id — use this to accept or remove.

FriendLists.description: Your friendships split by what the UI does with each one.

incoming.description: Pending requests other people sent you.

createdBy.description: Null on a private group you are not in — the group is findable, but who is in it is not.

viewerRole.description: The caller's role, or null when they are not a member.

viewerStatus.description: Where the caller stands with this group: in it, invited and yet to answer, waiting on an admin, or nothing at all.

canRead.description: False for a private group you are not in: its posts and its member list answer 403. The fields above are still yours to render.

status.description: In the group, asked in, or asking to come in.

joinedAt.description: When the row was made — the invite or request date while pending.

invitedBy.description: Who sent the invitation, on an invited row.

GroupInvitation.description: A group waiting on your answer.

role.description: Only meaningful in a group chat.

lastReadAt.description: How far this person has read — use it to show read receipts.

title.description: What to show in the inbox: the group name, or the other person’s name in a direct chat.

avatarUrl.description: The group picture, or the other person’s avatar.

name.description: The stored group name; empty for direct chats.

lastMessageAt.description: What the inbox is sorted by.

lastMessage.description: The preview line under the title.

viewerRole.description: Your role in a group chat.

replyTo.description: The id of the message this one answers.

editedAt.description: Set once the sender edits it.

deleted.description: True for an unsent message. It keeps its place in the thread with empty text, so the client can render "Message unsent".

canEdit.description: Yours, still standing, and inside the 15-minute window. The client shows the Edit control on this rather than keeping its own clock.

canUnsend.description: The same rule, for Remove for everyone.

type.description: A text story carries no media and usually a background.

text.description: The caption on media, or the whole story without it.

background.description: Text stories only: a CSS background for the client to paint.

expiresAt.description: 24 hours after it went up. Past this it stops being readable.

seen.description: Whether the caller has already watched it.

viewCount.description: Your own stories only — absent on everyone else's.

StoryGroup.description: One person's live stories, which is how the rail renders them.

isViewer.description: True on your own group, which sorts first.

hasUnseen.description: What the highlighted ring in the rail keys off.

items.description: Oldest first — the order they play in.

Notification.description: Something that happened to you. The client words it from `type`; `post`, `comment` and `group` are filled in for the types that have one, and are null when that thing has since been deleted.

delete.description: A soft delete: the row stays in the database with status "inactive". Login and every existing token stop working immediately. Posts are kept.

example.message: User not found.

put.description: Signs you out everywhere else: every token issued before the change stops working, over REST and on open sockets. The response carries a fresh token for this session.

get.description: Newest first. A reel is a post with type "reel", so the same endpoint serves both feeds.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Only this author. Used by the profile page.

parameters.name: groupId
parameters.description: A group's feed. Omit it for the main feed, which excludes group posts. A private group is members-only.

post.description: Upload media first with POST /upload, then send the URLs it returns. A reel needs exactly one video; a post needs text or at least one file.

groupId.description: Posts into a group. You have to be a member of it.

get.description: What a notification links to. A post in a private group is only returned to its members.

patch.summary: Edit your own post or reel
patch.description: Text only — media cannot be swapped after publishing. An edit that would leave the post with no text and no media is rejected.

delete.summary: Delete your own post or reel
delete.description: Any photo or video on it is deleted from Cloudinary at the same time, so the file stops being served rather than living on at its URL. Media that did not come from this account is left alone. A provider failure is logged and does not undo the delete.

put.description: One reaction per person per post, so calling this again replaces the previous one rather than adding another. likeCount mirrors how many people reacted.

type.description: The client maps names to numbers: 1 like, 2 love, 3 care, 4 haha, 5 wow, 6 sad, 7 angry.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: A post id for GET and POST, a comment id for DELETE.

get.summary: List the comments on a post or reel
get.description: `id` is the **post** id. Oldest first. A post with no comments returns an empty array, not a 404.

post.description: `id` is the **post** id. Also bumps the post's commentCount.

delete.description: `id` is the **comment** id. Only the author may delete, and the post's commentCount goes back down.

get.description: Searches both directions, so requests you received show up under `incoming` and ones you sent under `outgoing`.
Active accounts you are not already connected to in either direction, newest first.

post.description: Refused if you target yourself, if the account does not exist, or if a request already exists in either direction.

409.description: A request already exists between you two.

example.message: Friend request already exists

put.description: Only the person who received the request may answer it. Accepting raises both people's friendsCount, and only on a real change, so calling it twice does not double-count.

403.description: Only the recipient can answer a request.

example.message: Only the person who received this request can answer it.

delete.summary: Unfriend, decline a request, or cancel one you sent
delete.description: All three are the same operation: the row is removed. Only the two people involved may do it, and friendsCount only drops if the request had been accepted.

403.description: You are not part of this friendship.

example.message: You are not part of this friendship.

get.summary: Discover groups, or list your own
get.description:
By default returns groups you are **not** in, busiest first. Private groups appear too: you cannot read one, but you have to be able to find it before you can ask to join, so each carries `canRead: false` and a `viewerStatus` of `"requested"` once you have asked.

Groups that have invited you are left out; they are under `GET /groups/invitations`. Pass `mine=true` for the groups you belong to.

parameters.name: mine
parameters.description: true returns your groups instead of suggestions.

post.description: You become its first member, with the admin role.

get.description: Anyone signed in can read a group card: name, cover, description and member count. On a private group you are not in, `canRead` is false and `createdBy` is null, its posts and member list are closed, and `viewerStatus` says whether you have already asked to join.

patch.description: Admins only. Switching a private group to **public** lets everyone with a pending join request in at the same time — the only thing their request was waiting on was the group being private.

403.description: You are not an admin of this group.

example.message: Only a group admin can do that.

delete.description: Admins only. Removes the group, every membership and every post in it, along with any photos and videos those posts carried on Cloudinary.

403.description: You are not an admin of this group.

example.message: Only a group admin can do that.

get.summary: List the members, the invitations or the requests
get.description:
Admins first. The member list of a private group is members-only.

`status=invited` returns people who have been asked in and have not answered, which any member may look at. `status=requested` returns the join requests waiting on an admin, and only an admin may look at those.

post.summary: Join a group, or ask to join a private one
post.description:
A public group lets you straight in. A private one files a request for its admins to answer. If the group had already invited you, this accepts that invitation, and a request left over from when a now-public group was private is simply let in. Read `status` in the reply to know which happened.

Two joins for the same person at once cannot both succeed — the database keeps one and the other answers 409.

201.description: You are in, or your request was filed.

status.description: active means you are in; requested means an admin has to answer.

409.description: You are already in, or have already asked.

example.message: You have already asked to join this group.

delete.description: The only remaining admin cannot leave — promote someone else or delete the group.

example.message: You are the only admin. Make someone else an admin, or delete the group.

get.description: Invitations other people have sent you, newest first. Accept one with `PATCH /groups/{id}/members/{yourId}`, turn it down with `DELETE` on the same path.

post.description:
Any member can ask people in, and this is the only way into a private group besides a request. Nobody is added by it: each person gets an invitation to accept or turn down. Anyone already in, or already invited, is skipped.

Someone who has already **asked** to join is a different case, because answering a request is an admin's decision. An admin inviting them lets them straight in (`approved`). A plain member inviting them does not — they are skipped and listed in `awaitingAdmin`, so a member cannot use an invitation to get around admin approval.

approved.description: Had already asked to join and went straight in. Admins only.

awaitingAdmin.description: Had already asked to join, but the caller is not an admin, so their request is left for an admin to answer.

403.description: You are not in this group.

example.message: Only members of this group can do that.
They are already in this group, or already invited.

put.summary: Make someone an admin, or take it back
put.description: Admins only, and only on people who are actually in the group. Two people can never lose the role: the creator, and whoever is the last admin left — a group with no admin can no longer be edited or cleaned up. That is also how the only admin gets out: make someone else an admin first, then leave.

400.description: Unknown role, or this is the last admin.

example.message: A group needs at least one admin. Make someone else an admin first.

403.description: You are not an admin, or the target is the creator.

example.message: The group creator is always an admin.
That person is not in this group.
They are already an admin.

patch.summary: Accept an invitation, or approve a join request
patch.description: Both end in the same place, so one call covers them and who you are decides which it is: pass your **own** id to accept an invitation the group sent you, or somebody else id, as an admin, to let their request in.

403.description: Not your invitation, or you are not an admin.

example.message: Only the person invited can accept an invitation.
There is nothing to answer here.
That person is already in this group.

delete.summary: Remove a member, or take away an invitation or a request

403.description: Not an admin, or the target is the creator.

example.message: The group creator cannot be removed.

get.description: Chats you are in, most recently active first, each with its last message, its participants and your own unread count. Chats you have deleted are left out until someone sends to them again.

post.summary: Open a direct chat, or start a group chat
post.description:
Send `{ "userId": "..." }` to open a one-to-one chat. This is idempotent: if the thread already exists you get it back with **200** instead of a duplicate, so the client can call it every time the user presses Message.

Send `{ "type": "group", "participantIds": [...] }` for a group chat. You become its admin, and it needs at least two other people.

participantIds.description: Everyone but you — you are added automatically.

404.description: One of those accounts is gone or deactivated.

example.message: One of those accounts no longer exists.

get.summary: Unread totals for the message badge
get.description: How many chats are unread, and how many messages that adds up to. Clients on the realtime socket refetch this after reconnecting instead of polling it.
The chat header: title, picture, participants and your unread count.

404.description: No such chat, or you are not in it — both answer 404 so private threads are not leaked.

example.message: Conversation not found.

patch.description: Group chats only, admins only. A direct chat is named after the other person.

400.description: This is a direct chat, or the name is too long.

example.message: That only applies to group chats.

403.description: You are not an admin of this chat.

example.message: Only a chat admin can do that.

404.description: No such chat, or you are not in it — both answer 404 so private threads are not leaked.

example.message: Conversation not found.

delete.summary: Delete a chat, for you only
delete.description: Hides the chat and everything said in it so far from your inbox. Everyone else keeps the thread, and the next message brings it back for you with only the new messages in it. To walk out of a group chat for good, use `DELETE /conversations/{id}/participants`.

404.description: No such chat, or you are not in it — both answer 404 so private threads are not leaked.

example.message: Conversation not found.

post.description: Clears your unread count for this chat. Call it when the thread is opened.

404.description: No such chat, or you are not in it — both answer 404 so private threads are not leaked.

example.message: Conversation not found.

get.description:
Newest message first. To page backwards through the history, pass the `nextCursor` from the previous call as `before`; a null `nextCursor` means you have reached the start of the thread.

New, edited and unsent messages are pushed over the `/ws` socket as `message:new` and `message:updated`, in this same shape. Call this again after reconnecting to pick up anything sent while the socket was down.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: A message id: return only messages older than it.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `before` for the next page; null at the start of the thread.

404.description: No such chat, or you are not in it — both answer 404 so private threads are not leaked.

example.message: Conversation not found.

post.description: A message needs text, at least one attachment, or both. Attachments are the objects `POST /upload` returns, passed straight through.

replyTo.description: The id of a message in this same chat.

404.description: No such chat, or you are not in it — both answer 404 so private threads are not leaked.

example.message: Conversation not found.

patch.description: Your own messages only, only the text (attachments stay as they were sent), and only within **15 minutes** of sending. Past that the message is part of a shared record and the call answers 400. The reply carries `editedAt` so the client can mark it as edited.

example.message: You can only change your own messages.

delete.summary: Remove a message, for you or for everyone
delete.description:
Two different acts behind one call, chosen with `scope`.

**`scope=me`** takes the message off your own thread and nobody else's. Any message qualifies, including one somebody else sent and one already unsent — hiding something from yourself takes nothing from anyone else, which is what stops one person clearing another's history. No time limit, and it cannot be undone.

**`scope=everyone`** (the default) unsends it. Your own messages only, and only within **15 minutes** of sending. The row stays as a tombstone — `deleted: true` with empty text — so the thread keeps its order and replies keep a target. Any photo or video is deleted from Cloudinary at the same time; if that provider call fails the message is still unsent and the failure is logged.

example.message: You can only remove a message within 15 minutes of sending it.

403.description: Not your message — only for scope=everyone.

example.message: You can only change your own messages.

get.summary: List the people in a chat

404.description: No such chat, or you are not in it — both answer 404 so private threads are not leaked.

example.message: Conversation not found.

post.summary: Add people to a group chat
post.description: Any member can add. A direct chat cannot grow — start a group chat instead. Anyone already in the chat is skipped.

400.description: This is a direct chat, or the chat is full.

example.message: You cannot add people to a direct chat. Start a group chat instead.

404.description: No such chat, or you are not in it — both answer 404 so private threads are not leaked.

example.message: Conversation not found.

409.description: They are already in the chat.

example.message: They are already in this chat.

delete.description: Group chats only. If you were the last admin, the longest-standing member takes over; if you were the last person, the chat and its messages are removed.

example.message: You cannot leave a direct chat. Delete it instead.

404.description: No such chat, or you are not in it — both answer 404 so private threads are not leaked.

example.message: Conversation not found.

delete.summary: Remove someone from a group chat
delete.description: Admins only. Use leave to remove yourself.

403.description: You are not an admin of this chat.

example.message: Only a chat admin can do that.

404.description: No such chat, or you are not in it — both answer 404 so private threads are not leaked.

example.message: Conversation not found.

get.description:
Live stories from you and your friends, grouped by the person who posted them and ordered the way the rail reads: you first, then anyone with something you have not seen, then the rest by recency. Inside a group the stories run oldest to newest, which is the order they play in.

`viewCount` appears only on your own stories — how many people watched is the author's business.

post.description: Either a picture or video — pass the descriptor `POST /upload` returned — or a text story with an optional background. A caption may ride along with media. Every story lapses 24 hours after it goes up.

media.description: Leave this out for a text story.

text.description: The caption on media, or the whole story without it.

background.description: Text stories only: any CSS background the client understands.

get.description: Newest first, each with the number of people who have watched it.

post.description: Call it when the story opens. One view per person however many times they come back, and looking at your own story never counts — the number is meant to say how many other people watched.

counted.description: False when this was a repeat look, or your own story.

404.description: Expired, deleted, or posted by someone whose stories you do not see — all three answer the same way, so a story you are not meant to know about stays unknown.

example.message: That story is no longer available.

get.description: Newest first. Only the person who posted it may ask.

example.message: Only the person who posted a story can see who watched it.

404.description: Expired, deleted, or posted by someone whose stories you do not see — all three answer the same way, so a story you are not meant to know about stays unknown.

example.message: That story is no longer available.

delete.description: Takes the story, its view rows and its picture on Cloudinary. Your own only.

example.message: You can only delete your own stories.

404.description: Expired, deleted, or posted by someone whose stories you do not see — all three answer the same way, so a story you are not meant to know about stays unknown.

example.message: That story is no longer available.

post.summary: Send images and videos to Cloudinary
post.description: Multipart form data under the field name `media`, up to 6 files at once. Images must be under 10MB, videos under 100MB. Nothing is written to the server disk — the files are streamed straight through. Use the URLs it returns when creating a post, a reel, an avatar or a cover photo.

400.description: Wrong file type, too many files, or a file over the size cap.

example.message: clip.txt is not an image or video.

errors.media: Only image and video files can be uploaded.

delete.summary: Throw away files that were uploaded but never used

skipped.description: Not yours, already claimed, or still referenced.

get.description:
Newest first, 20 at a time. Pass the previous `nextCursor` as `before` for the next page; a null cursor means there is nothing older. `unread` is the badge number.

Created for: friend requests sent to you and accepted, comments and first reactions on your posts, and group invitations. Chat messages are not notifications — they have their own badge under `/conversations/unread`.

get.summary: Unread count for the bell badge

200.description: Marked read. `unread` is the new badge number.
